quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The first golden rays of sunrise peeking over the hills"?
quests.hint: Think about what a sunrise actually marks the beginning of.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunrise marks the very start of the day.
quests.funFact: No two sunrises ever look exactly the same, because clouds and air change every morning!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The sky fading from orange to deep purple, then finally to black"?
quests.hint: Think about what color the sky ends up once it finishes fading.
quests.explanation: Yes! Once the sky finishes fading all the way to black, night has begun.
quests.funFact: This colorful fading happens because the sun's light has to travel through more of the sky as it sets!

quests.instruction: "A rooster crowing just as the sky begins to brighten" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about a sky 'beginning to brighten' — what is it turning into?
quests.explanation: Yes! A brightening sky signals the day is just beginning.
quests.funFact: Roosters are famous for crowing right as the sun begins to rise!

quests.instruction: "The very last sliver of sun disappearing below the horizon" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what happens the moment the sun is completely gone from view.
quests.explanation: Yes! Once the sun has completely disappeared below the horizon, night begins.
quests.funFact: This exact moment is called sunset, the official start of night!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "The sun climbing slowly above the horizon". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about which direction the sun moves as morning begins.
quests.explanation: Yes! The sun climbs above the horizon as the day begins.
quests.funFact: It takes the sun only a couple of minutes to fully rise above the horizon!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Streetlamps flickering to life as darkness settles in". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what 'darkness settles in' is telling you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Streetlamps turn on as darkness settles in, at the start of night.
quests.funFact: Many streetlamps use a light sensor to switch on automatically as it grows dark!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Early morning fog lifting as the sun rises". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about what the sun's warmth slowly does to morning fog.
quests.explanation: Yes! As the sun rises and warms the air, morning fog begins to lift.
quests.funFact: Fog is really just a cloud that forms close to the ground!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The sky completely black, with the first stars appearing"?
quests.hint: Think about what a completely black sky, dotted with stars, tells you.
quests.explanation: Yes! A black sky with stars appearing is a clear sign that night has arrived.
quests.funFact: The very brightest stars are usually the first ones you can spot as the sky darkens!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The sky turning pink and orange as the sun comes up"?
quests.hint: Think about what 'as the sun comes up' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! A pink and orange sky like this happens as the sun rises, starting the day.
quests.funFact: Sunrise colors happen because sunlight bends and scatters through the morning air!

quests.instruction: "A family closing the curtains as the last daylight fades away" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what 'the last daylight fades away' tells you.
quests.explanation: Yes! Once the last daylight fades away, night has begun.
quests.funFact: Closing curtains at night can help keep a home's warmth from escaping!

quests.instruction: "Dew sparkling on the grass in the early morning light" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'early morning' — which part of the day is that?
quests.explanation: Yes! Early morning is part of the daytime, right after the sun rises.
quests.funFact: Dew forms overnight, but it usually sparkles brightest once morning light hits it!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Bats leaving their roost just as darkness falls". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about what 'darkness falls' means for the time of day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bats leave their roost right as darkness falls, at the start of night.
quests.funFact: Some bat colonies can have millions of bats all living together!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Farmers heading out to the fields as the sun rises". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what happens right as the sun rises — the day begins!
quests.explanation: Yes! Farmers often start their fieldwork right as the sun comes up, beginning the day.
quests.funFact: Many farmers get an early start so they can finish outdoor work before the hottest part of the day!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The moon rising as the very last light disappears from the sky"?
quests.hint: Think about what it means for the very last light to disappear.
quests.explanation: Yes! Once the last daylight disappears and the moon rises, night has fully begun.
quests.funFact: The moon doesn't always rise at the exact same time every single night!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "The sun still low in the sky, casting long morning shadows". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when the sun is low but has already risen.
quests.explanation: Yes! A low sun still counts as daytime — it has already risen and the day has begun.
quests.funFact: Shadows are longest in the early morning and late afternoon, when the sun is lower in the sky!

quests.instruction: "Crickets starting their nightly song as darkness takes over" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what 'darkness takes over' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Crickets begin singing once darkness takes over the sky.
quests.funFact: Crickets chirp faster when it's warmer outside and slower when it's cooler!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A teacher writing today's lesson on the whiteboard"?
quests.hint: Think about when teachers are usually in the classroom, teaching lessons.
quests.explanation: Yes! Teachers work in the classroom during school hours, in the daytime.
quests.funFact: Whiteboards became popular because they were easier to clean than old chalkboards!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A security guard beginning her overnight shift at the museum". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'overnight' — when does that shift take place?
quests.explanation: Yes! An overnight shift takes place through the night, while most people sleep.
quests.funFact: Museums use security guards and alarms to help protect valuable art and artifacts!

quests.instruction: "A doctor examining patients in a busy clinic" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when most clinics are open for regular appointments.
quests.explanation: Yes! Most clinics are open and busy with patients during the day.
quests.funFact: Doctors train for many years before they're ready to care for patients on their own!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "An astronomer setting up a telescope after the sky turns dark"?
quests.hint: Think about when the sky needs to be dark for stargazing to work well.
quests.explanation: Yes! Astronomers need a dark sky to see the stars clearly, so this happens at night.
quests.funFact: Some astronomers travel to very remote places, far from city lights, to see the clearest night skies!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A chef chopping vegetables in a bustling kitchen". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when restaurant kitchens are busiest, preparing food for meals.
quests.explanation: Yes! Many chefs prepare food throughout the day, getting ready for meals.
quests.funFact: Professional chefs train for years to learn how to chop vegetables quickly and safely!

quests.instruction: "A baker beginning to knead dough long before sunrise" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what 'before sunrise' tells you — has the day started yet?
quests.explanation: Yes! 'Before sunrise' means the day hasn't started yet, so this is still nighttime.
quests.funFact: Some bakers start working many hours before sunrise so fresh bread is ready first thing in the morning!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A firefighter washing the fire truck outside the station". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when it's easiest to see the truck clearly while cleaning it.
quests.explanation: Yes! Cleaning and checking equipment is often a daytime task at the fire station.
quests.funFact: Firefighters keep their trucks spotless so every tool is easy to find in an emergency!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A nurse checking on patients during her overnight shift in a quiet hospital hallway". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when a hospital hallway would be this quiet, with most visitors gone.
quests.explanation: Yes! A night-shift nurse works through the night, caring for patients while most people sleep.
quests.funFact: Hospitals need caring staff working around the clock, both day and night, to help patients!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A librarian stamping due dates into borrowed books"?
quests.hint: Think about when libraries are usually open to the public.
quests.explanation: Yes! Libraries are typically open and busy with visitors during the day.
quests.funFact: Some libraries still use their classic due-date stamps, even though most systems are now digital!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A DJ playing music for a crowd dancing under string lights"?
quests.hint: Think about when string lights are usually turned on to glow and sparkle.
quests.explanation: Yes! String lights glow best once it's dark, so parties like this usually happen at night.
quests.funFact: String lights use tiny bulbs that use very little electricity to shine!

quests.instruction: "A bus driver greeting passengers at each stop" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when most people are out and about, riding the bus to get places.
quests.explanation: Yes! Most bus routes run throughout the day, carrying passengers to their destinations.
quests.funFact: Some city buses can carry over 100 passengers at once!

quests.instruction: "A truck driver navigating dark highways with headlights on" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when headlights are actually needed to see the road.
quests.explanation: Yes! Headlights are needed to see clearly once it's dark outside.
quests.funFact: Some truck drivers travel through the night to deliver goods before morning!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A veterinarian checking a puppy's health at the clinic". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when most pet clinics are open for regular checkups.
quests.explanation: Yes! Most veterinary clinics are open for checkups during the day.
quests.funFact: Veterinarians care for all kinds of animals, from tiny hamsters to giant horses!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A lighthouse keeper making sure the beacon shines brightly". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when ships need a bright, shining light to guide them safely.
quests.explanation: Yes! Lighthouse beacons shine brightest at night, guiding ships safely through the dark.
quests.funFact: Some lighthouses have been guiding ships safely for hundreds of years!
